evidence.field: image identity, form provenance, and rights
evidence.text: The file page describes ACC-b18630.svg as a digitally created vector depicting 二 in Western Zhou bronze-script style. It links this rendering to Xiaoxuetang form 33.F82B and identifies its source context as 免簋 (mid-Western Zhou). The page states that the Sinica Database picture is under CC0 1.0. This is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:ACC-b18630.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The notice states that glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the website’s query interface are dedicated under CC0 1.0. It does not establish rights to unrelated linked material or wholesale database reuse.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形演變資料庫版權聲明

evidence.text: The CC0 deed describes a worldwide waiver of copyright and related rights to the extent allowed by law and permits copying, modification, and distribution. The Commons file page applies CC0 to this rendering and attributes the depicted source picture to the Sinica Database.
evidence.title: CC0 1.0 Universal - Creative Commons

search_audit.query: 二 Western Zhou bronze 免簋 ACC-b18630 Wikimedia Commons
search_audit.outcome: Search results identified the Commons file page. Opened and inspected its description, which identifies the image as a modern vector rendering of 二 in Western Zhou bronze-script style and notes a mid-Western Zhou 免簋 context.

Opened the Commons page and confirmed it exposes the exact original-file link https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4e/ACC-b18630.svg. The web opener could not access the direct SVG URL. Opened and inspected the CC0 deed and Xiaoxuetang rights notice. The exact Xiaoxuetang character record page was inaccessible to the web opener; its query page URL is included as provenance as specified by the Commons file page.

gaps: The direct SVG URL was exposed on the Commons page but could not be opened by the web tool. The Commons description and file history support the candidate identity and rights; the underlying pixels were not visually inspected in this research.

The Xiaoxuetang character record page could not be opened directly in this session. The Commons file description links the exact 二 record and identifies form 33.F82B; the Xiaoxuetang rights notice itself was accessible.
No direct dated inscription artifact photograph was identified or verified here; the candidate is explicitly a modern vector redraw of a Western Zhou bronze-style form.

items.source_title: 小學堂字形演變資料庫 record for 二
items.period: Mid-Western Zhou, as identified by the Commons description for the 免簋 example
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 二 in Western Zhou bronze-script style, linked to the mid-Western Zhou 免簋 example; it shows the two-stroke numeral graph.
items.alt: Two horizontal strokes, the upper shorter than the lower, drawn in a Western Zhou bronze-script style.
items.selection_reason: The Commons page identifies this specific redraw as 二, names the 免簋 context, and links form 33.F82B on the Xiaoxuetang 二 record. It provides a sourced historical-style example relevant to the simple two-stroke graph.
items.rights: CC0 1.0, as stated for the Sinica Database picture on the Commons file page and in the Xiaoxuetang query-interface rights notice.

limitations.text: The candidate is a digitally created vector redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The direct SVG and Xiaoxuetang record could not be opened by the web tool, so visual inspection and independent verification against the underlying inscription were not performed.
